Oakridge needs low p95 for real-time fraud scoring and wants a benchmark on H100 vs A100. Security and VPC/KMS questions were raised. Agreed next steps: run benchmarks, share security docs, schedule technical deep dive, and provide pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), John Rivera (Oakridge CTO), Priya Singh (Oakridge ML Eng), Carlos Mendez (Oakridge Infra), Rina Patel (Oakridge Product)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - I'm Maya, AE on the account. Liam our SE will handle the latency / benchmarking questions.
[00:15] John (Oakridge CTO): Hi all, John here. We're evaluating options, mainly because our fraud scoring path needs to be realtime, p95 under 300ms ideally for short responses.
[00:30] Priya (Oakridge): Yeah, and we do both classification-ish prompts (short < 64 tokens) and longer explainers (~200-400 tokens) for case reviews. Concurrency is around 200 sustained, spike to 500 during peak.
[00:50] Liam (Redwood SE): Got it. Quick clarifying Q - when you say p95 under 300ms, is that first-token latency or end-to-end for a 32-64 token response?
[01:05] John: Mostly first-token and end-to-end for short outputs. First-token is critical - UI must feel instant. For the longer explainers we can tolerate up to 1.5s p95.
[01:20] Carlos (Oakridge Infra): Network note - our infra is in GCP us-west2, we are ok with regionally hosted but need VPC peering or private link for Dedicated/Private. Also KMS for keys, must keep logs audit-able.
[01:40] Maya: Makes sense. High level - Redwood Hosted can meet low-latency for many workloads, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control and compliance. For p95 targets and concurrency we usually recommend running a workload-specific benchmark because token/sec and latency vary a lot by model, sequence length, and batching behavior.
[02:05] Liam: To add - we often see first-token latency on H100-backed Dedicated endpoints ~60-150ms for small prompt sizes depending on model and quantization. End-to-end for 64 tokens often falls in 200-400ms p95 if batching is tuned. But those are numbers, you know, ballpark - we should run the exact test with your prompts.
[02:30] Priya: That helps. What about streaming? We need token-by-token streaming for our UI. First-token matters, but streaming reduces perceived latency for long responses.
[02:45] Liam: Redwood supports streaming and function-style outputs. Streaming first token latencies are similar to regular first-token; the benefit is perceived latency. For throughput, continuous batching and KV prefix cache can increase tokens/sec and reduce cost.
[03:05] John: On cost - we're evaluating unit economics. If we go Dedicated, what's the typical cost per 1M tokens vs hosted?
[03:15] Maya: I'll send the detailed pricing sheet. Short answer: Dedicated committed capacity drops unit cost significantly once you fill the slots, but you have to commit. Hosted is simple consumption but higher per-token. We'll include a model comparing your expected QPS and token length.
[03:30] Carlos: For benchmarking, can you run on both H100 and A100 images? We have internal biases toward H100 but want a concrete comparison for token/sec and p95.
[03:45] Liam: Yes - we can run parallel benchmarks. Our plan: synthetic load tests at 50, 200, 500 concurrent, streaming and non-streaming, using your sample prompts. We'll report p50/p95/p99 for first-token and end-to-end, plus tokens/sec and GPU utilization.
[04:05] Priya: Are there any gotchas with warm vs cold caches? We rely on prefixing the conversation and expected to reuse contexts across calls.
[04:15] Liam: Warm caches matter. We'll run both cold and warmed KV cache runs. With warmed KV/prefix caching you can see significant tail latency improvements. We'll document the cache hit rates in the report.
[04:30] John: Security checklist: SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS, VPC peering, audit logs. We might need an on-prem option later for regulated flows. Can Redwood support that?
[04:45] Maya: Yes - Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem. We have SOC2 and SAML support. I'll include the security package and the SOC2 report.
[05:00] Carlos: What about data retention and logs? We need to ensure no PII persists unless explicitly logged and to control retention windows.
[05:10] Maya: You can configure retention and opt-out of data retention on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has configurable retention policies too; we'll include the specifics.
[05:25] Rina (Oakridge Product): From product side we care about error modes and graceful degradation - if the endpoint is under load what fallbacks do we have?
[05:35] Liam: We offer smart routing and fallback policies - route to cheaper model variants or to lower-quality quantized variants. Also rate limiting and automatic burst capacity options for Dedicated. We'll demo rollback and A/B routing in a technical session.
[05:55] John: For the benchmark parameters - let's define SLOs: p95 first-token under 300ms for <64 tokens; p95 end-to-end under 1.5s for 200-400 tokens. Concurrency 200 sustained, spike 500. Streaming required.
[06:20] Liam: Noted. We'll run: (1) first-token latency test for small prompts, (2) end-to-end for medium prompts, (3) streaming test, (4) sustained throughput for tokens/sec across concurrency levels.
[06:35] Priya: Any constraints on input encoding or rate-limits that change numbers? We do a mix of nested JSON prompts and long metadata prefaces.
[06:45] Liam: Complex prompt preprocessing can add client-side latency but server-side tokenization and model compute remain the primary contributors. We'll include a tokenization delta in the bench.
[07:00] Maya: Quick re: competitors - you mentioned internal stack and Anthropic; anything else in scope?
[07:08] John: OpenAI is also considered; we want to quantify latency / cost differences versus a managed vendor and vs our in-house infra.
[07:16] Liam: We'll make sure to include rough comparative baselines if you want; but we'll focus first on absolute numbers for your workload.
[07:30] Carlos: For the Dedicated pool sizing - what's the mapping between concurrency and GPU counts? E.g., for your typical 4 token/sec per request type how many GPUs do we need for 200 concurrency?
[07:45] Liam: It depends on model and token/sec per GPU. As a rough calc: if a GPU can do 4k tokens/sec on your model, and each request averages 64 tokens, that's ~62.5 requests/sec per GPU. For 200 concurrent at, say, 2 requests/sec per user that's 400 rps -> you'd need ~6-7 GPUs. We'll run exact sizing in the bench.
[08:10] Priya: Could you also measure cost per 1k predictions, so we can plug into ROI?
[08:20] Maya: Yes - bench will include unit economics per model / per deployment option.
[08:30] John: About canary/rollouts - we want to do A/B for model versions and have automated fallback to previous versions on regressions.
[08:40] Liam: Redwood supports canaries and automatic fallback with traffic split and rollbacks. We can demo that during the technical deep dive.
[08:55] Rina: Do you have observability hooks? We need token-level latency breakdown and tracing.
[09:05] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll share example screenshots and the retention options.
[09:20] John: Ok, timeline - we'd like to run benchmarks this week and get results by EOW. Is that feasible?
[09:30] Liam: We can start as soon as we have your prompt set and traffic profile. For thorough runs across H100 and A100 and warm/cold caches it'll take 3-5 business days. So EOW is tight but possible if you share artifacts today.
[09:50] Carlos: We'll share prompt set and a csv of traffic distribution by EOD.
[10:00] Maya: Next steps recap - I'll send SOC2/security docs and pricing; Liam will run benchmarks; schedule tech deep dive with Carlos; and we'll follow up with results and a recommended deployment path.
[10:18] John: Sounds good. One more question - if Dedicated increases concurrency but we still hit tail latency, what are options?
[10:30] Liam: Options: increase reserved GPUs, pick a lower-latency model variant, enable more aggressive caching, or use shorter context by truncation. Also parallelize requests where possible. We'll document tradeoffs in the bench report.
[10:50] Priya: For the bench, include both streaming and non-streaming token throughput numbers and GPU utilization so we can see cost/latency tradeoffs.
[11:05] Liam: Affirmative. We'll include p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and per-1k predictions cost.
[11:20] Maya: Great - thanks everyone. We'll circulate the notes and action items.
[11:30] John: Thanks all.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings - "Redwood Dedicate" appears in a couple places, product names occasionally uneven; some filler 'um' and 'yeah' removed for brevity.)
